verdicts.reasoning: Hungry Hobby's recipe adds vinegar, soy sauce/coconut aminos, peppercorns, brown sugar, bay leaves, onion, and garlic to the slow cooker. Bay leaves (along with whole peppercorns) are a standard, essential adobo aromatic that our list omits entirely - not just a stylistic variation of the soy/vinegar/garlic base.

Rachel Cooks whisks olive oil, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, garlic, dried oregano, lemon zest, salt, onion powder, and pepper as the marinade. Oregano is the defining herb of a Greek marinade and is completely absent from our ingredient list.

Eating on a Dime's mojo sauce combines orange juice, lime juice, garlic, oregano, salt, pepper, cumin, corn starch, cilantro, and mint. Oregano is a core mojo criollo seasoning (alongside cumin, which we already have) and is missing from our list.

Betty Crocker's recipe mixes the cannellini beans, onions, and bell pepper with 1 tablespoon of Italian seasoning before cooking. This seasoning blend (oregano/basil/etc.) is what makes the dish 'Italian' and is entirely absent from our stored ingredients, which otherwise just list the raw vegetables, beans, tomatoes, and cheese.
